draft.title: Women in Sparta
card: Spartan girls were encouraged to exercise. Ancient writers say they trained in running, wrestling and throwing, so that they would be strong and healthy.
Spartan women could own land. Ancient writers say that over time women came to hold a large share of Spartan land, and they could pass property on to their children.
Men spent much of their lives in the army or in training, so women often ran the household and its estate.

Most of our sources were written by men, and many came from outside Sparta. Even so, they agree that Spartan women had more freedom than women in Athens, who had far fewer property rights and a life more tied to the home.
draft.remember: Spartan women exercised, owned land and ran households, which gave them more freedom than Athenian women.

a.q: Which feature of Spartan life most helps explain why women ran households and estates?
opts: Men spent much of their lives in the army or training
Women were barred from owning any property at all
Women had to live inside separate quarters at home
Helots were forbidden from working on the estates
a.why: Men were often away serving the state, so women managed the household and estate. The claim that women could not own property is wrong: Spartan women could own land, and that is part of why they had more freedom.
a.clue: Think about where Spartan men spent much of their time.

b.q: A historian compares a Spartan woman with an Athenian woman of the same period. Which comparison is supported by the ancient sources?
opts: The Spartan woman had more freedom, including owning land
The Athenian woman had more freedom, including owning land
Both women had equal freedom, as both ran estates
Neither woman had any freedom, as both lived in seclusion
b.why: Ancient writers agree that Spartan women could own land and move more freely than Athenian women. Athenian women had far fewer property rights, so the claim that they had more freedom reverses the comparison.
b.clue: Which city let women own land and exercise?

a.best: Men spent much of their lives in the army or training

b.best: The Spartan woman had more freedom, including owning land
